jasimuddin-mela.desc: Every January, around the poet's birth anniversary, a fair is held at Ambikapur near Jasimuddin's home. Stalls sell clay toys, nakshi kantha, sweets and household goods, while stages host folk songs, jatra and poetry readings. It draws families from across the region for several days. It is one of the best chances to experience a traditional rural mela in central Bangladesh.

glance: Faridpur town fish markets and local eateries
faridpur-padma-ilish.desc: Faridpur's northern edge runs along the Padma, one of the most prized hilsa rivers. Locals swear by the rich, oily flavour of Padma hilsa in mustard gravy or steamed in banana leaf. In the monsoon and early autumn, fish markets in Faridpur town are full of silver fish. Avoid buying during the official breeding-season ban, when fishing is prohibited.

glance: 120 km to Faridpur by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
faridpur-padma-chars.desc: North of Faridpur town, the Padma spreads wide, with chars that shift every year with the floods. In late autumn, some are covered in white kash grass flowers that wave in the wind. Local boatmen from the riverside ghats can take you across for a walk on the sand. It is simple, open and peaceful, a very different side of the district.
blocks: How to get there
Auto from Faridpur town to a Padma ghat on the north side, then hire a boat.
Good to know
Agree fares first, carry water and sun cover, and avoid rough weather.

glance: 120 km to Faridpur by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
jasimuddin-house-ambikapur.desc: Jasimuddin, author of Nakshi Kanthar Math, grew up in Ambikapur village just outside Faridpur town. His family's simple tin-roofed homestead has been preserved, and a museum nearby displays his books, letters and photographs. The poet asked to be buried near the old pomegranate tree in the family graveyard, and his wish was kept. Walking down to the Kumar river helps you see the scenery he wrote about.
blocks: How to get there
Rickshaw or auto from Faridpur town to Ambikapur, about 15 minutes.
Good to know
Visit in January to coincide with the Jasimuddin fair.

faridpur-jute.desc: Faridpur is one of Bangladesh's leading jute districts, and the crop shapes village life from July to September. Farmers cut the tall stalks, sink them in ponds and canals to ret, then strip the fibre by hand. Golden bundles hang drying on bamboo frames and bridges, and the stripped sticks are used for fuel and fencing. The smell of retting jute is part of the season.
blocks: Good to know
Ask before photographing people working; the best scenes are on rural roads early morning.

pathrail-mosque-bhanga.desc: The Pathrail Mosque, also called the Majlis Aulia Mosque, stands in Bhanga upazila beside the shrine of Majlis Abdullah Khan. Its long prayer hall, about 22 metres by 9, is roofed with ten domes of equal height, and the walls carry rectangular terracotta panels with floral scrolls and rosettes. It is usually dated to the 15th or early 16th century and is compared with the Choto Sona and Bagha mosques. A large old water tank lies beside it. Few travellers on the new Bhanga expressway know it is so close.
blocks: How to get there
From Bhanga go east about 8 km along the Bhanga–Mawa road to Polia, then take an auto or van about 4 km south to Pathrail.
Good to know
It is an active mosque, so visit outside prayer times and dress modestly. Combine it with a stop at the Bhanga interchange on the way back.

glance: Pure gur roughly 300–600 BDT per kg; much cheaper gur is usually mixed with sugar
Makers in villages around Faridpur Sadar such as Bishnupur, and winter haats and sweet shops in Faridpur town
faridpur-khejur-gur.desc: Faridpur has long been one of the main date-palm gur districts. From late autumn, gachhis tap the trees at dusk, collect the sap at dawn and boil it down into liquid jhola gur or set patali. Villages such as Bishnupur in Sadar upazila are known for a pale, high-quality gur, and local sweet makers turn the new season's gur into sandesh and pitha. Date trees are getting scarcer and adulterated gur is common, so buy from makers or trusted sellers.

glance: Established sweet shops in central Faridpur town
winter (Dec–Jan), spring (Feb–Mar), summer (Apr–May), monsoon (Jun–Jul), autumn (Aug–Sep) and late autumn (Oct–Nov)
faridpur-malaikari.desc: Faridpur is long associated with malaikari, a soft chhana sweet served in rich, thickened cream. It is milder and creamier than rasmalai, and good versions taste strongly of fresh milk. Sweet shops in Faridpur town also sell khir chomchom and other milk sweets. Buy it fresh and eat it the same day.

glance: 120 km to Faridpur by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
munshi-abdur-rouf-museum.desc: Munshi Abdur Rouf was a soldier of the East Pakistan Rifles who held off a Pakistani attack with his machine gun at Burighat in Rangamati in April 1971, giving his comrades time to pull back, and was killed there. He is one of the seven Bir Sreshtho, Bangladesh's highest gallantry award. This museum and library stand in his home village, Salamatpur in Madhukhali upazila, now also called Raufnagar. It is a modest place with photographs and information about his life and the war, and a reading room for local people.
blocks: How to get there
Bus from Faridpur town towards Madhukhali, then a CNG or easy-bike to Salamatpur (Raufnagar).
Good to know
It is a small village museum; combine it with Jasimuddin's house or the Mathurapur Deul for a full day out from Faridpur.

glance: About 750 BDT per kg, or 40 BDT a piece (2026)
Gobinda Mistanna Bhandar on Chitarbazar Main Road, Boalmari, and its branch in Kondardia village (about 8 km away)
winter (Dec–Jan), spring (Feb–Mar), summer (Apr–May), monsoon (Jun–Jul), autumn (Aug–Sep) and late autumn (Oct–Nov)
boalmari-ilish-peti.desc: Ilish peti is a sweet made from pure khir and shaped like the belly cut of a hilsa, which gave it its name. It was first made by Gobinda Kundu's shop in Boalmari upazila and caught on quickly because of its look as much as its taste. It is the costliest of the 15 or so sweets the shop makes each day. The family now runs two branches, one on Chitarbazar Main Road in Boalmari and one in Kondardia village.

glance: 120 km to Faridpur by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
mathurapur-deul.desc: Mathurapur Deul is a slender, multi-faceted brick tower in Madhukhali upazila, thought to date from the 17th century. Its sides are ribbed and decorated with terracotta panels of figures and floral designs. There are competing local stories about who built it, and its exact purpose is debated. Standing alone near the Chandana river, it is one of the most striking monuments in southern Bengal.
blocks: How to get there
Bus from Faridpur town to Madhukhali, then an auto to Mathurapur.

glance: 120 km to Faridpur by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
sri-angan-faridpur.desc: Sri Angan, in the Goalchamot area of Faridpur town, is the ashram of Prabhu Jagadbandhu, a Hindu holy man of the late 19th and early 20th centuries whose teaching inspired the Mahanam Sampradaya. He spent much of his life meditating and preaching here, and devotees come from across Bangladesh and India, especially for his birth anniversary. On 21 April 1971 the Pakistani army entered the ashram and killed eight monks who were chanting inside; a memorial remembers them. The compound is calm, with temples, a courtyard and the steady sound of kirtan.
blocks: How to get there
Rickshaw or auto from anywhere in Faridpur town to Goalchamot; Sri Angan is well known locally.
Good to know
Take off your shoes inside the temple area and keep your voice low during kirtan. Ask before photographing worshippers.

glance: 120 km to Faridpur by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
satoir-mosque.desc: Satoir Mosque in Boalmari upazila is a domed brick mosque attributed to the Bengal Sultanate period in the early 16th century. Its plain, solid walls and corner towers are typical of the period. It has been restored over the years and is still used for prayer.
blocks: How to get there
Bus from Faridpur town to Boalmari, then an auto to Satoir.
Good to know
Visit outside prayer times and dress modestly.
